name: Early Winter
description:
Choose one —
• Exile target creature.
• Exile target enchantment an opponent controls.
assumptions: Node B (`move`, `self`, `stack`→`gy`) was treated as the spell's ordinary post-resolution trip to its owner's graveyard, not as printed text — the schema explicitly lists "a resolved spell's own resting zone" as a valid use of `move`, so I read it as structural bookkeeping rather than an effect the card states.

Root `A` (the `cast` node) has no continuation besides that resting-zone move, so I assumed it contributes no visible rules text of its own (no flashback/buyback/alternate cost) — the only self-registry entry and the only `cast` node both point to a single plain hand-cast.
Rendered the `combine: 1` root as a "Choose one —" bulleted modal, per the schema's own statement that "a number N means a genuine modal choice ('choose one —' is N=1)".

Node D (`owner:opp`, `thing:enchantment`, `flags:target`) is structurally identical in shape to node C (`owner:any`, `thing:creature`, `flags:target`), which is unambiguously "exile target creature" — so I read D the same way, as the caster directly targeting and choosing a specific enchantment controlled by an opponent, and worded it "exile target enchantment an opponent controls."
couldNotDerive: Supertype and rarity: neither the self registry nor any node supplies these (rarity is explicitly withheld in the file), so both are omitted from the type line rather than guessed.

Whether the second mode's legal target is the enchantment itself (as I assumed) or the opposing player, with that player then choosing which of their own enchantments is affected — `flags:target` on node D doesn't distinguish "object is the target, caster picks it" from "player is the target, that player picks the object," so I could not confirm which shape this is and defaulted to the same reading as node C.
notes:
Second attempt, post-fix. Real card (forge-model/data/early-winter.txt): SP$ Charm with two DB$ ChangeZone modes. Mode 1 (DBChangeZone1: ValidTgts$ Creature, Origin$ Battlefield, Destination$ Exile) = 'Exile target creature.' Node C reproduces this exactly (owner:any, thing:creature, flags:target) — unchanged from attempt 1, no issue.

Mode 2 (DBChangeZone2: Origin$ Battlefield, Destination$ Exile, ValidTgts$ Opponent, DefinedPlayer$ Targeted, ChangeType$ Enchantment, ChangeNum$ 1, Chooser$ Targeted, Mandatory$ True) = 'Target opponent exiles an enchantment they control.' Node D is now owner:opp, thing:enchantment, flags:target. This confirms the translator fix described going into this attempt: ValidTgts$ Opponent (a bare player predicate) is no longer mis-read as the object-type/owner string 'opponent' (the pre-fix bug produced owner:any, thing:"opponent", which the attempt-1 blind agent correctly flagged as uninterpretable and refused to guess at); ChangeType$ Enchantment now correctly supplies the moved-object type, and the owner-from-target-predicate logic now correctly resolves the bare player predicate to owner:opp. Node D's field values are exactly what the pre-fix attempt's root-cause notes predicted the corrected node should look like.

With node D now well-formed, this blind reconstruction produced a coherent, fully-specified mode 2 ('Exile target enchantment an opponent controls') instead of the prior attempt's 'could not derive' placeholder — a real improvement, and the schema/edge data is faithful as far as it goes.

Remaining, narrower gap (the one flagged as deliberately deferred going in): the schema's flags vocabulary has no way to distinguish 'the object is the legal target, and the caster picks which one' (mode 1's real shape, and node C's shape) from 'the PLAYER is the legal target, and that player — not the caster — picks which of their own qualifying objects is affected' (mode 2's real shape: ValidTgts$ Opponent + DefinedPlayer$ Targeted + Chooser$ Targeted). Because node D is structurally identical to node C (owner + thing + flags:target, nothing marking who chooses), a faithful reconstruction from the nodes alone lands on 'exile target enchantment an opponent controls' rather than the real 'target opponent exiles an enchantment they control.' These diverge concretely when the opponent controls zero or multiple enchantments (my reading requires a legal enchantment target to exist at all; the real card always has a legal target — the opponent — and only asks them to choose/exile if they control one, per Mandatory$ True on their own choice) and on whose decision picks the specific permanent. fields.Chooser is still never read anywhere in forgeTranslate.ts — the fix that landed repaired the object-type/owner derivation (ChangeType$ vs ValidTgts$ precedence, and the bare-player-predicate case in the owner regex), not the chooser semantics; nothing in the current flags vocabulary (e.g. no `chooser:` value) could express it yet even if the translator did read Chooser$. This is exactly the 'opponent, not caster, chooses which enchantment' nuance called out as a known, deliberately deferred gap for this attempt, not a new regression or a fault of this reconstruction.

Overall: modal structure (root A + combine:1 of [C,D], A→B) is correct and was never in question. Mode 1 is an exact match. Mode 2's node data is now correct at the level the schema can express; only the caster-vs-targeted-player chooser distinction remains unrepresentable, which is the specific, narrow issue this verdict reflects.
